title: ADAS — Agentic depth & tool frontier
description: How deep agentic work goes, what it costs, how often it fails, and which internal systems it reaches through MCP. Built on dial_usage_log aggregated per trace_id - the turns rollup is deliberately not used, and avoiding it also removes turns' chat-id restriction, which leaves out every trace without a chat id. Served by ADAS (POST /v1/queries/execute-sql) — never by a direct ClickHouse datasource; ReplacingMergeTree deduplication (FINAL) is applied server-side.

panels.title: Read this before trusting a number

options.content:
**A turn is one `trace_id`, aggregated from raw `dial_usage_log` hops** — not the `turns` rollup, which no dashboard reads.

**Why not the rollup: coverage.** `turns` is restricted to hops carrying a `chat_id`, and much traffic carries none, so a rollup-based view of this dashboard's questions could describe only a minority of traffic. Counting hops directly also keeps `hop_count` honest: Core's entry row is included rather than filtered away.

**Per turn vs in total.** A deep turn can cost far more *per turn* than a one-hop turn and still be a small slice of total spend, because deep turns are rare. Read 'Dollar per turn' against 'Cost $' in the depth-bands table: where the shallow bands — single-hop turns and the 2-3 hop routed-chain band (a router or app plus the model it calls) — carry most of the spend, optimise the common call, not the spectacular chain. The depth-bands table is the live source and this note is only a reading guide.

**Failure need not be monotonic in depth.** 'Failure %' is per turn, and a turn with more hops has more chances to fail, so multi-hop bands can fail more often than single-hop ones — but the rate need not keep rising with depth, and the deep bands are often too small to read as rates. Do not claim a clean depth-to-failure curve from this.

**Latency is per hop, not per turn.** `operation_duration_ms` is a hop's wall clock and a parent's duration contains its children's, so hop latencies cannot be summed into a turn duration. The tool leaderboard's p95 is therefore per MCP call, which is the honest unit. **'MCP requests' counts every `event_kind = 'mcp'` hop**, protocol traffic (`initialize`, `tools/list`, …) included; only the hops that carry an `mcp_tool_call_name` are what the tool leaderboard's `Calls` counts — so the two figures can differ widely by definition, not by error.

**Served by ADAS, never by a direct ClickHouse datasource.** Every panel on this dashboard goes through `POST /v1/queries/execute-sql`, so it runs inside the governed pipeline: entity and field validation, a closed function catalog, per-column visibility, and a hard **1,000-row cap** per result. **Deduplication is the service's job** — `FINAL` is applied server-side, so there is no raw-read inflation to guard against here. **`deployment_price`, not `total_price`** for usage-log cost: it is a hop's own cost, so summing it over hops does not double-count a routed chain.

**Four properties of ADAS's SQL surface shape every panel's SQL** (the dialect in full: `docs/sql-reference.md`). (1) There are no `$__timeFilter` / `$__timeInterval` macros — the range is interpolated as `TIMESTAMP` literals from Grafana's own `__from` / `__to` globals via their `:date:` formatter, and buckets are fixed-width `date_bin(n, unit, col)`, so **bucket width does not follow panel width**. (2) Enrichment tables are never joined — they are read as dotted columns on the spine (`usage_client_identity.client_type`, `session_insights.activity`), which never drops a spine row: in a plain single-entity statement like every query here, a missing enrichment row reads the column's type default (`''` for a non-nullable string), not NULL — NULL is what an unmatched side yields inside an explicit join, and these panels use none, which is why coverage is tested with `<> ''`. (3) an `enum` column can be *compared* with a string literal directly (`= 'x'`, `<> 'x'`, `IN (…)`), but cannot be *produced* alongside one — `coalesce(enum, 'none')` or a `CASE` returning either is rejected once the result is grouped, so those go through `to_string()` first. (4) `countIf` / `uniqExactIf` / `multiIf` / `quantile` have no direct equivalent; they are `count(CASE WHEN ...)`, `count(DISTINCT CASE WHEN ...)`, `CASE WHEN`, and `percentile_cont(p) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY col)` — which renders to the same ClickHouse `quantile()` — a reservoir estimate on both sides, so p95 values match the original exactly while both can sit a few percent off the exact percentile on groups above ~8k values.

panels.title: Agentic shape
panels.description: One turn is one trace_id, aggregated from raw dial_usage_log hops over the dashboard window - no chat-id restriction, so this is the whole population, not the 'turns' rollup's slice. 'Deep' is more than 10 hops. The gap between the average hop count and the deepest turn is the point: a near-1 average against a very deep maximum means the distribution has a very long tail, and the tail is where the per-turn cost lives (see the depth bands below). 'MCP requests' counts every hop with event_kind = 'mcp', protocol traffic such as initialize and tools/list included, so it can run well above the number of real tool invocations; 'Turns using tools' and 'Distinct tools' count only hops that carry an mcp_tool_call_name. 'Turns with a chat id %' is the coverage the retired trace-grain rollup would have limited every number on this dashboard to.

url_options.data: {"sql": "SELECT count(*) AS \"Turns\", round(sum(hops) * 1.0 / count(*), 2) AS \"Avg hops\", max(hops) AS \"Deepest turn (hops)\", count(CASE WHEN hops > 10 THEN 1 END) AS \"Deep turns (>10 hops)\", sum(mcp_hops) AS \"MCP requests\", count(CASE WHEN tool_hops > 0 THEN 1 END) AS \"Turns using tools\", (SELECT count(DISTINCT mcp_tool_call_name) FROM dial_usage_log WHERE request_time >= TIMESTAMP '${__from:date:YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss}' AND request_time < TIMESTAMP '${__to:date:YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss}' AND mcp_tool_call_name <> '') AS \"Distinct tools\", round(100.0 * count(CASE WHEN chat_hops > 0 THEN 1 END) / count(*), 1) AS \"Turns with a chat id %\" FROM (SELECT trace_id, count(*) AS hops, count(CASE WHEN event_kind = 'mcp' THEN 1 END) AS mcp_hops, count(CASE WHEN mcp_tool_call_name <> '' THEN 1 END) AS tool_hops, count(CASE WHEN chat_id <> '' THEN 1 END) AS chat_hops FROM dial_usage_log WHERE request_time >= TIMESTAMP '${__from:date:YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss}' AND request_time < TIMESTAMP '${__to:date:YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss}' GROUP BY trace_id)"}

panels.title: Depth bands — cost per turn and share of spend
panels.description: One row per depth band. A turn is one trace_id, aggregated from raw dial_usage_log hops in the dashboard window; cost is deployment_price (a hop's own cost, so summing over hops does not double-count a routed chain). Sorted by 'Dollar per turn' descending, so the priciest class per turn is on top. Read the two cost columns together: 'Dollar per turn' says deep turns are extravagant, while 'Cost $' says where the budget actually sits, which is often the shallow bands. 'Failure %' is the share of turns with at least one unsuccessful hop, a per-turn rate and not a per-hop one.

url_options.data: {"sql": "SELECT CASE WHEN hops <= 1 THEN '1 hop' WHEN hops <= 3 THEN '2-3 hops' WHEN hops <= 10 THEN '4-10 hops' WHEN hops <= 50 THEN '11-50 hops' WHEN hops <= 200 THEN '51-200 hops' ELSE '200+ hops' END AS \"Depth band\", count(*) AS \"Turns\", sum(llm_calls) AS \"LLM calls\", sum(mcp_calls) AS \"MCP calls\", round(sum(cost), 2) AS \"Cost $\", round(sum(cost) / count(*), 4) AS \"Dollar per turn\", round(100.0 * count(CASE WHEN failed > 0 THEN 1 END) / count(*), 2) AS \"Failure %\" FROM (SELECT trace_id, count(*) AS hops, count(CASE WHEN event_kind = 'llm_call' THEN 1 END) AS llm_calls, count(CASE WHEN event_kind = 'mcp' THEN 1 END) AS mcp_calls, count(CASE WHEN success = false THEN 1 END) AS failed, sum(deployment_price) AS cost FROM dial_usage_log WHERE request_time >= TIMESTAMP '${__from:date:YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss}' AND request_time < TIMESTAMP '${__to:date:YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss}' GROUP BY trace_id) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 6 DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 200"}

panels.title: MCP tool leaderboard — what AI reaches into
panels.description: One row per MCP tool, straight from mcp_tool_call_name at hop grain (every row with a tool name is an event_kind = 'mcp' hop). This is the most direct answer to 'which internal systems is AI using'. 'Calls' counts MCP hops, 'Turns' distinct trace_ids that made at least one such call, 'Servers' the distinct deployments (toolsets) serving that tool name, 'Failed' the hops with success = false. p95 is per tool call, which is the honest unit for latency — a parent hop's duration contains its children's, so these cannot be summed into a turn. Rows arrive sorted by Calls; click the p95 header to find the slow integrations. Capped at 300 tools; if the table shows exactly 300 rows, the tail is hidden.

url_options.data: {"sql": "SELECT mcp_tool_call_name AS \"Tool\", count(*) AS \"Calls\", count(DISTINCT trace_id) AS \"Turns\", count(DISTINCT deployment) AS \"Servers\", round(percentile_cont(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY operation_duration_ms)) AS \"p95 ms\", count(CASE WHEN success = false THEN 1 END) AS \"Failed\" FROM dial_usage_log WHERE request_time >= TIMESTAMP '${__from:date:YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss}' AND request_time < TIMESTAMP '${__to:date:YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss}' AND mcp_tool_call_name <> '' AND mcp_tool_call_name IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 300"}

panels.title: LLM calls vs MCP calls over time
panels.description: LLM-call and MCP hops per hour, stacked. Only two of the five event_kind values are plotted — embedding, blank and route are excluded, so the stack height is a subset of gateway hops, not total traffic. MCP rising relative to LLM is the signal that agentic tool use is growing; 'MCP calls' is every MCP-protocol hop and not all of them carry a tool name, so it is a wider population than the tool leaderboard's Calls. Spiky by nature — one deep turn can contribute hundreds of MCP calls. Fixed 1-hour buckets: ADAS has no $__timeInterval macro, so bucket width follows neither the panel width nor the selected range.

url_options.data: {"sql": "SELECT date_bin(1, 'hour', request_time) AS ts, count(CASE WHEN event_kind = 'llm_call' THEN 1 END) AS \"LLM calls\", count(CASE WHEN event_kind = 'mcp' THEN 1 END) AS \"MCP calls\" FROM dial_usage_log WHERE request_time >= TIMESTAMP '${__from:date:YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss}' AND request_time < TIMESTAMP '${__to:date:YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss}' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1 LIMIT 1000"}

panels.title: Deepest turns — drill-down
panels.description: Top 200 turns by hop count (a turn is one trace_id) over the dashboard window. Hops counts every usage-log hop in the trace — llm_call, mcp, embedding, route and Core's own entry row — so LLM calls + MCP calls is normally less than Hops. Cost $ sums deployment_price, each hop's own cost, so a routed chain is not double-counted. An empty Conversation means no hop of the turn carried a chat id: exactly the population the old turns-based version could not see. Tools used and Models billed list the alphabetically first 6 distinct entries; Tools gives the real distinct-tool count, so you can see when that list is truncated. Sorted by depth, not by cost: the most expensive turn in a window need not be among the deepest, so it may NOT be in this table.

url_options.data: {"sql": "SELECT trace_id AS \"Trace\", max(chat_id) AS \"Conversation\", count(*) AS \"Hops\", count(CASE WHEN event_kind = 'llm_call' THEN 1 END) AS \"LLM calls\", count(CASE WHEN event_kind = 'mcp' THEN 1 END) AS \"MCP calls\", count(CASE WHEN success = false THEN 1 END) AS \"Failed hops\", count(DISTINCT CASE WHEN mcp_tool_call_name <> '' THEN mcp_tool_call_name END) AS \"Tools\", array_to_string(array_slice(group_uniq_array(CASE WHEN mcp_tool_call_name <> '' THEN mcp_tool_call_name END), 1, 6), ', ') AS \"Tools used\", array_to_string(array_slice(group_uniq_array(CASE WHEN deployment_price > 0 THEN deployment END), 1, 6), ', ') AS \"Models billed\", round(sum(deployment_price), 4) AS \"Cost $\" FROM dial_usage_log WHERE request_time >= TIMESTAMP '${__from:date:YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss}' AND request_time < TIMESTAMP '${__to:date:YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss}' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 3 DESC NULLS LAST, 1 LIMIT 200"}
